'''David C. Kelly''' (1940–2025) was a professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Hampshire College]] in [[Amherst, Massachusetts]]. Kelly founded and directed the [[Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics]] program (HCSSiM) for talented high-school students.

==Early life and education==
Kelly was originally from [[New Rochelle, New York]], but moved frequently as the child of a military father. He held an AB degree from [[Princeton University|Princeton]], an SM from [[MIT]] (after stopping out from a doctoral program there) and an AM from [[Dartmouth College|Dartmouth]].<ref name=mourns/>

==Career and later life==
Kelly taught at [[Talladega College]], [[New College of Florida|New College]] and [[Oberlin College]] before joining Hampshire College in 1970 as one of its founding faculty members. After ten years of teaching summer math programs at [[St. Paul's School (New Hampshire)|St. Paul's School]] and [[University of New Hampshire]], in 1971 he founded the Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics, an annual six-week program for mathematically talented high-school students. He continued to direct the program until his death.<ref name=mourns/>

He died on June 10, 2025, shortly before his 85th birthday. He was survived by his husband of 17 years and partner of 51 years, Al McNeely.<ref name="mourns">{{cite web|url=https://www.hampshire.edu/news/hampshire-college-mourns-founding-faculty-member-david-c-kelly|title=Hampshire College Mourns Founding Faculty Member David C. Kelly|first=Karen|last=Corday|publisher=Hampshire College|date=August 11, 2025|access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>

==Yellow pigs and 17==
[[File:YellowPigsDayCake2004.JPG|thumb|right|Yellow Pigs Day cake (2004)]]
After meeting as Princeton students in the early 1960s, later in the decade Kelly and fellow mathematician [[Michael Spivak]] created "[[Yellow Pigs Day]]," an annual celebration of mathematics and the number [[17 (number)|17]]. The HCSSiM program organizes the holiday each year on July 17, commemorating the day with a reunion, mathematics, food and songs. Kelly was expertly familiar with the properties of the number 17, and gave a special lecture on the subject each summer.<ref name="crimson">{{cite news | first=Laura A. | last=Haight | title=Hamming It Up At Hampshire: Mathematics Gone Hogwild | work=[[Harvard Crimson]] | date=1982-02-05 | url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/1982/2/5/hamming-it-up-at-hampshire-pisaturday/ | access-date=2026-08-14 |quote=Fisher: In Princeton about 30 years ago. [''[[sic]]'': implausible at age 11]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Will '17 be the Year of the Pig? |url=https://mathenchant.wordpress.com/2016/12/10/will-17-be-the-year-of-the-pig/ |first=James |last=Propp |author-link=James Propp |work=Mathematical Enchantments |date=December 10, 2016 |access-date=August 15, 2026 |quote=straight from Kelly: 'Mike Spivak was a grad student while I was an undergraduate at Princeton; we didn't know each other particularly well until I got him to teach in my 2 UNH programs. The Yellow Pig dates from those later years [1968–1969].'}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=Kelly is quoted by an expert mathematician. This is permitted by [[WP:Blog]], but ideally the historical info would be sourced from a professionally reviewed publication.|date=August 2026}}<ref>{{cite web |title=The HCSSiM Yellow Pig Songbook |url=https://www.yellowpigs.net/yellowpigs/songs/ |first=Sara |last=Smollett |work=YellowPigs.net |access-date=August 15, 2026}}</ref>

When Kelly retired from the faculty in 2015, Hampshire College officially changed the campus speed limit to 17&nbsp;mph in his honor, reflecting his lifelong fascination with the number.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.masslive.com/news/2015/10/17-mph_hampshire_college_speed_limit_honors_math_prof.html |title=Hampshire College honors retiring math professor David Kelly with 17 mph speed limit signs |first=Carolyn  |last=Robbins |work=MassLive |date=October 16, 2015 |access-date=August 14, 2026}}</ref>

==Legacy and recognition==
Kelly was well known for his inquiry-based teaching style. He often used the phrases "Interesting, if true" and "Let's find out" to encourage students to explore mathematical ideas.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://admin.aimath.org/resources/how-to-run-a-math-camp/participantlist/ |title=How to Run a Math Camp |publisher=American Institute of Mathematics |date=March 6, 2013 |access-date=August 31, 2026}}</ref> Through his leadership at [[Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics|HCSSiM]], he fostered a unique mathematical community that influenced generations of students.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Blackwood |first=Kate |date=2026-03-17 |title='Hunting Yellow Pigs' film shows a singular approach to math education |url=https://math.cornell.edu/news/hunting-yellow-pigs-film-shows-singular-approach-math-education |access-date=2026-05-02 |publisher=Cornell University}}</ref> Kelly was elected to the 2026 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], but died before he could celebrate this honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2026 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>

===''Hunting Yellow Pigs'' documentary===
In 2026, the feature-length documentary ''[[Hunting Yellow Pigs]]'' was officially released. Directed by HCSSiM alumnus '''Jon Roberts''', who executive-produced with '''Ming-I Huang''', the film explores the unique community and "questions-first" philosophy that Kelly established at HCSSiM. It includes interviews with dozens of prominent mathematicians and alumni, including [[Eric Lander]], [[Lisa Randall]], [[Steven Strogatz]] and [[Lisa Su]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |date=2026 |title=Cast |url=https://www.huntingyellowpigs.com/cast |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=Hunting Yellow Pigs}}</ref> and chronicles the program's quirky traditions and its influence on American mathematics education.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=''Hunting Yellow Pigs'' |url=https://www.ypmathfoundation.org/hunting-yellow-pigs |access-date=2026-05-02 |publisher=YP Math Foundation}}</ref> The film was selected as "Best Documentary" by Tokyo's Golden Harvest Film Festival.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goldenhff.com/ |title=Best Documentary Film Award: ''Hunting Yellow Pigs'' |publisher=Golden Harvest Film Festival |date=2026 |access-date=August 26, 2026}}</ref>
